title: Memorial Hall
text: “Above all, it depicts something like a knight order showing up afterward, saying they’ll protect the world, and then vanishing—and after that, no more waves occur.”
“But one’s happening right now. Doesn’t that mean it’s completely fake, since it doesn’t match?”
“Voff, that’s exactly why I think it got disposed of, and only this one copy survived.”
“Isn’t it just old garbage, then?”
“Voffff…”
No, wait, I say. Let me recall. What was it that Ark said again?
『I made the mastermind behind this whole incident’s world pay the price. There shouldn’t be any more waves around here now.』

『The one in charge tried to make some excuse or other, but honestly, it was almost funny how they assumed we wouldn’t dig up the truth. That whole world was rotten to the core, on a systemic level. From their perspective, I probably look like nothing but a slaughterer.』

Now that I think of it, I recall Ark grumbling something else too—about how someone claimed to be protecting this world despite everything. I have no idea what position the Crimson Swine itself held in all this, but… somehow, my instincts whispered to me that the book was telling the truth, I say. There’s no way someone as thick-headed as you could sense that! says Father from the first world in my memories, but my instincts are never wrong, indeed.
“Even so, it’s a proud old book. A single volume that survived through repeated wars.”
“Huh, books like that exist, huh.”
“Voff, an item that overcame the erasure of history itself.”
“Oh, I’ve heard something like that too. Riska and the others told me—apparently a lot of old records get lost during major conflicts.”

“That’s right. Strangely enough, it’s often the case that whichever king or queen, or the people close to them, or whoever became the Hero at the time, spread new technology and adopted a policy of ‘don’t look back at the past,’ disposing of records in the process. There are even cases where whole nations vanished after demon summonings.”
“Ah, that’s apparently the work of the mastermind behind the waves, secretly erasing anything inconvenient for the Heroes, I say.”
“Gaelion-san and Rafumi mentioned that too. The natives who are my roots went through the same thing.”
In the end, it all comes down to the schemes of whoever’s orchestrating the waves, I say.
“Who knows how much of it was actually true…”
“There’s plenty more inside. If you’re interested, feel free to read it anytime. Treat it like it’s your own house.”

“In a sense, I guess that makes it a book from a family with real history. I’m not that much of a researcher though… honestly, more importantly, what am I even supposed to do with myself once everything’s over?”
Father, talking about after the waves end.
“Voff, by all means, come to the castle in Siltvelt—the Shield Hero is Siltvelt’s hope.”
“No, no, wouldn’t it be nice to just relax in Seaetto territory instead? Things sound like they’d get exhausting over there.”
“The nobles of Shieldfreeden also seemed like they wanted you to come.”
Father certainly has plenty of offers on the table, indeed. Of course, he could go to Faubrey too.
“I’ll think about it. So… is this the end of exploring Wolf’s house?”
“Voffff! There’s still so much more to see. There’s even a training ground, so everyone could train together, and honestly, you could remodel the castle however you like.”
“That does sound fun. Is the money situation okay, though?”
Wolf nodded firmly.
“Quite a bit of aid money came in from Siltvelt. Repairs are being considered too.”
“I bet.”

“And also… Takt’s inheritance got liquidated, so there’s a huge amount of settlement money now. His relatives are eyeing it like vultures, so I sort of have to spend it before they get their hands on it.”
Wow, that sounds like a hassle, Father said, sympathizing with Wolf.
“Heh, I won’t let them interfere. I’ll just punch them quiet.”
“So brute force works there, huh. Well, I’ll just call it ‘Wolf’s skillful handling’ then.”
“Voff.”

Well, thanks to how deftly she’s been managing things, I imagine the rumors about Wolf—something about letting her brother die to become the Claw Hero—are probably the sort of nasty gossip being spread around.
“Still, though… considering the atmosphere around Wolf’s hometown region and all that, if we renovated the castle into like, a hotel, wouldn’t that be pretty stylish?”
“It’d become like a castle in some revitalized tourist district, I say.”
“Ahh…”
At my one remark, Father made a troubled sort of noise.
“Was that no good?”

“No, Motoyasu-kun, I am now completely convinced that idea would fail. Yeah. I can just tell that turning Wolf’s house into a hotel would flop. There’s no beating that place. Now that I think about it, it already looked like some kind of tourist spot to begin with.”

There’s already plenty of bustle there, after all. Above all, if we fairies keep going out to play too much in our current forms, this world’s future risks turning into something just like the previous world, which would limit our options going forward, indeed.
“I guess if you say it resembles something, it does resemble something.”

“But there’s no ‘pioneer fairy’ element involved, so wouldn’t that be fine? Even if you turn Wolf’s house into a hotel, if you built something like a Claw Hero Memorial Hall, wouldn’t people come? Other countries have them, don’t they?”
“Such things exist…? Buildings like that?”

Well, yes, they do exist, I say. Sort of archive-type buildings left behind by past generations of Heroes. Even in countries where a Phoenix is sealed away, there are buildings recording things like ‘how to defeat the Phoenix,’ along with various other records—in a sense, those count as Hero Memorial Halls too, I say. Incidentally, memorial halls for Takt opened up in both Faubrey and Shieldfreeden, but they got demolished almost instantly, indeed. Disgusting, honestly. To think that man was running a business like that. I’ve never actually seen inside myself, but according to Itsuki and Father, who did look through it, there were exhibits related to firearms, cars, and airplanes, apparently.
“I wonder if memorial halls will eventually get built for us too…”
“Of course they will, indeed! I intend to personally open a memorial hall for Father and Filo-tan, and show it to the world, I say.”

In the first world, such things were built absolutely everywhere. I can vaguely recall one even existing in Zeltoble. Of course, I think there were also articles covering the damage from Rafumi’s rampages.
“Motoyasu-kun, what exactly are you saying? What in the world do you plan to display in my memorial hall?”
“Whether we actually open one or not aside, it might be nice to compile some records regardless.”
“Right. Based on the Spear Hero’s testimony, drafting up some documents might not be a bad idea, you know? If we opened branches in different countries, it could even turn a profit.”
“Voff.”
With a click, even Wolf pulled out a pair of glasses and something that looked suspiciously like an abacus, and started calculating away, indeed.
“Wait, hold on, everyone? Why is this suddenly coming together? Do you seriously think we could draw crowds when we haven’t even done anything all that impressive?”
“The waves are going to keep happening for a while yet, and there’s also the peacekeeping efforts across various countries to consider.”
“Plus there’s the work capturing all the troublemakers running rampant in different areas. The Bow Hero’s been gradually getting more famous too. We can’t exactly fall behind.”

“If we used activity reports and footage from things like the circus stuff Elena gathered, for publicity and exhibits, maybe Demi-Humans and Beastmen from various countries would come visit Seaetto as tourists. With tourism revenue coming in, reconstruction would speed up too.”
And so the slaves began earnestly discussing, in a rather forward-thinking manner, the matter of compiling records and building a memorial hall for Father, indeed.
“Of course, Yuki-chan too. Once you become famous through Filolial racing, you’ll get your very own solo memorial hall, indeed.”
“Ooh, that’s a little tempting, honestly.”

Actually, I remember from my loops that a memorial hall for Yuki-chan really did exist. That’s the kind of talented star Yuki-chan is destined to become in Zeltoble, after all. Ah, and speaking of Yuki-chan’s other possible self—as the White Swan, Yuki-chan had all sorts of fans. While I was away, apparently a fan came to visit the training grounds at the ranch, and Yuki-chan met them in Filolial form and gave them proper fan service. Apparently she’d thought I had come to visit during training, only to realize it was just a fan, but she handled them cheerfully all the same—though afterward, once the fan left, she supposedly turned around and intimidated the Filolial breeders in a foul mood. They said White Swan Yuki-chan’s temper rivals Black Thunder’s. Though of course, nothing like that has ever happened with me, not even slightly. Well, there was that one time she asked me to personally ride and compete in the jockey-mounted category of Filolial racing. Though due to regulation restrictions, I was over the weight limit, so there were races I couldn’t actually enter.
“Everyone’s really developing a knack for business, huh.”
“Watching you, Iwatani-sama, it rubs off on people a little.”
“I wonder how a memorial hall for me specifically would even turn out, honestly.”
“Back in the first world, once peace finally came, there was actually a proposal floating around to build a giant statue of Father visible from anywhere, I say.”
For some reason, that plan quietly died out, indeed.
